GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3167 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
INTEGRATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY 
3167.  SHRI MANAS RANJAN MANGARAJ: 
 SHRI SUJEET KUMAR: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the steps being taken by Government to ensure variable renewable energy integration in the 
inter-connected national grid; 
 
(b
) the steps being  taken to ensure that the DISCOM clears their dues to power generation 
companies;  
 
(c) whether Government has issued any advisory to States to ensure that they do not renege from 
already negotiated power purchase agreements, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d
) whether Government has taken or has proposed to take some steps towards making people 
aware of the renewable sources of energy; and 
 
(e) the percentage of houses which have installed solar panels on their rooftops under any 
Central schemes? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) 
: The steps taken by the Central Government to facilitate Renewable Energy (RE) integration 
in the National Inter-connected Grid include :  
 
i. Construction of Intra-State and Inter-State transmission systems for evacuation of Renewable 
power. 
 
ii. Transmission plan for integration of more than 500 GW RE capacity by 2030 has been 
prepared. 
 
iii. Setting up of Regional Energy Management Centers (REMCs) for better forecasting of 
renewable power and to assist grid operators to manage variability and intermittency of 
renewable power. 
………2.
 
 
351

- 2 - 
 
iv. lnnovative products like Solar-Wind Hybrid Projects, RE projects with energy storage 
systems and supply of RE power balanced with power from non-RE sources launched to 
reduce intermittency. 
 
v. Flexibility in generation and Scheduling of Thermal/Hydro Power Stations through bundling 
with Renewable Energy and Storage Power. 
 
vi. Implementation of Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) and Green Day Ahead Market 
(GDAM) for sale of renewable energy. 
 
vii.
 Waiver of lnter-State Transmission Charges on transmission of electricity generated from 
Solar and Wind.
 
 
(b) : Following steps, inter-alia, have been taken to ensure that DISCOMs clear their dues to 
Power Generation Companies: 
 
i. Ministry of Power vide its Order No. 23/22/2019 -R&R dated 28.06.2019 has made it  
mandatory for Distribution Licensee s/Procurers of Power to open and maintain  adequate 
Letter of Credit (L oC) as Payment Security Mechanism under Power  Purchase Agreements 
(PPAs). As per the said Order, National Load Despatch Centre  (NLDC) and Regional Load 
Despatch Centre (RLDC) would dispatch powe r only after  it is intimated by Generating 
Company and/or Distribution Companies that L oC for  the desired quantum of power has 
been opened. 
 
ii. Ministry of Power has notified Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and Related Matters) 
Rules, 2022 on 03.06. 2022 in order to ensure payment discipline in the power sector value 
chain. These Rules entail obligations upon the DISCOMs to clear their legacy dues as 
existing on 03.06.2022, in a time bound phased manner in equated monthly installments with 
benefits of non-applicability of late payment surcharge after 03.06.2022. However, failure to 
repay the installment of legacy dues in accordance with the Rules would invite Late Payment 
Surcharge (LPS) on the entire outstanding amount. The LPS Rules also provide penal 
framework to ensure time bound clearance of current dues and establishment of Payment 
Security Mechanism as provided in PPA through disincentives of progressive withdrawal of 
open access as well as power regulation if the provisions of the Rules are not followed. 
DISCOMs can avail loans from PFC Ltd. and REC Ltd. to clear their legacy dues to 
Generating Companies. 
 
(c) :   Government from time to time have conveyed to States that contracts must be honoured. The 
Standard Bidding guidelines for Solar, Wind and Hybrid Projects have specific provision for 
termination compensation in case of unilateral termination of PPA. The guidelines also provide for a 
three-tier payment security mechanism by way of Letter of Credit, Payment Security Fund and Tri-
Partite Agreement (between the State Government, Reserve Bank of India and Government of 
India). 
 
(d) 
:  Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has undertaken various   awareness 
programmes  about the benefits of renewable energy through electronic, print and social media. 
 
(e) :   Under Rooftop Solar Programme of MNRE, 4.3 Lakh beneficiaries have installed solar panels 
on their rooftop.

RENEWABLE ENERGY 
 
3168. SHRI AJAY PRATAP SINGH 
 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of villages in the country which have been electrified with renewable 
energy; and 
(b) the number of industrial units in Madhya Pradesh for which energy audit has been done 
and the details of its process? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
(a) As reported by the States, all the inhabited un-electrified villages as per Census, 2011 stood 
electrified by 28th April, 2018 across the country. A total of 18,374 inhabited census villages 
were electrified under the scheme. Out of these villages, 2762 villages were electrified through 
Off-Grid mode.  
(b) As reported by Bureau of Energy Efficiency, total 52 industrial units in the state of Madhya 
Pradesh are covered under Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) Scheme as Designated entities  
and have undergone Mandatory Energy Audit as well as Monitoring and Verification Audit. 
In Energy Audit, plant equipment performance is assessed , the scope of energy efficiency 
improvement and energy conservation measures are explored and the same is recommended 
by the accredited energy auditor (AEA) for implementation. 
 
Monitoring and Verification (M&V) Audit is conducted under PAT scheme to verif y energy 
saving achieved during assessment year of the PAT Cycle comprises of three years duration. 
The M&V Audit is conducted by BEE Empanelled Accredited Energy Auditor (EmAEA) 
firms.

ANNEXURE-I REFFERED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) & (b) OF RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3169 FOR 28.03.2023 
DETAILS OF STEPS TAKEN TO PROMOTE RENEWABLE ENERGY 
INCLUDING SOLAR ENERGY IN THE COUNTRY 
• Permitting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) up to 100 percent under the automatic 
route. 
• Waiver of Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges for inter -state sale of 
solar and wind power for projects to be commissioned by 30th June 2025.  
• Declaration of trajectory for Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) up to the year 
2029-30.  
• Setting up of Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Parks to provide land and 
transmission to RE developers for installation of RE projects at large scale.  
• Schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evamUtthaanMahabhiyan 
(PM-KUSUM), Solar Rooftop Phase II, 12000 MW CPSU Scheme Phase II, etc. 
• Laying of new transmission lines and creating new sub -station capacity under the 
Green Energy Corridor Scheme for evacuation of renewable power. 
• Notification of standards for deployment of solar photovoltaic system/devices.  
• Setting up of Project Development Cell for attracting and facilitating investments. 
• Standard Bidding Guidelines for tariff based competitive bidding pro cess for 
procurement of Power from Grid Connected Solar PV and Wind Projects.  
• Government has issued orders that power shall be dispatched against Letter of 
Credit (LC) or advance payment to ensure timely payment by distribution licensees 
to RE generators. 
• Notification of Promoting Renewable Energy through Green Energy Open Access 
Rules 2022. 
• Notification of “The electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and related matters) Rules 
(LPS rules). 
• Launch of Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) to facilitate sale of Renewab le 
Energy Power through exchanges. 
• National Green Hydrogen Mission approved with an aim to make India a Global 
Hub for production, utilization and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
RAJYA SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3171 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
STATUS OF NATIONAL GREEN HYDROGEN MISSION 
3171. DR. ANIL JAIN 
 
Will the Minister of New and Renewable Energy be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) along with its 
characteristics; 
(b) the target of the mission by the year 2023; 
(c) the total amount being spent by Government towards the mission; 
(d) the details of the total investment planned for the mission; 
(e) the total number of employment aimed to be provided under the said scheme; and 
(f) to what extent the country's oil import is likely to be reduced due to the National Green 
Hydrogen Mission and Government expenditure likely to be saved on account of it? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
(a) to (e) On 4th January 2023, the Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission 
with an outlay of ₹ 19,744 crore. The overarching objective of the Mission is to make India the 
Global Hub for production, usage and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives,  by targeting 
production of 5 MMT per annum of Green Hydrogen by 2030. The following components have 
been announced as part of the Mission: 
 
(i)  Facilitating demand creation through exports and domestic utilization; 
(ii)  Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen  Transition (SIGHT) programme, which     
  includes incentives for manufacturing of electrolysers and production of green hydrogen;  
(iii)  Pilot Projects for steel, mobility, shipping, decentralized energy applications, hydrogen      
  production from biomass, hydrogen storage, etc.;    
(iv)   Development of Green Hydrogen Hubs; 
(v)   Support for infrastructure development; 
(vi)   Establishing a robust framework of regulations and standards; 
(vii) Research & Development programme including through a public -private partnership 
framework for R&D.  
      (viii) Skill development programme; and 
       (ix) Public awareness and outreach programme. 
 
The Green Hydrogen production capacity envisaged by 2030 is likely to leverage over ₹8 lakh 
crore in total investments in creating the Green Hydrogen ecosystem and create over 6 lakh jobs. 
(f) Crude oil imports can be reduced through use of green hydrogen as a fuel in mobility and 
shipping applications. U nder the Mission, only pilot projects are planned in these sectors. 
However, in other sectors such as fertilizer production and petroleum refining, green hydrogen 
production can substitute both domestic and imported natural gas.

FOREIGN AND DOMESTIC INVESTMENT IN NRE SECTOR 
 
3172. SHRI IRANNA KADADI 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of foreign and domestic investment in the New and Renewable Energy (NRE) sector in 
the country during the last four years and the current year, State-wise; 
(b) the details of the steps taken by Government to attract investments from both within the country 
and overseas with a view to add additional power and meeting the target set for the generation of 
power through renewable energy sources; and 
(c) whether any consultation has been held with the Ministry of Finance for providing certain 
additional incentives to this sector and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) Most of renewable energy projects in the country are being set up by private sector developers selected 
through a transparent bidding process. 
 
As per Global Status Report – Renewable 2022 published by REN21, the Investment trends in Indian 
Renewable Energy Sector during five calendar years are as follows:- 
 
Year Amount (Billion 
US$)

Further, the year-wise and state-wise details of Foreign Direct investment (FDI) Equity inflow reported 
in the Non-Conventional Energy sector since October 2019 till December 2022 are given in Annexure. 
 
(b) The Government has taken several measures to promote renewable energy in the country, including, 
inter-alia, the following:- 
 
• Permitting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) up to 100 percent under the automatic route,  
• Waiver of Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges for inter-state sale of solar and wind power 
for projects to be commissioned by 30th June 2025,  
• Declaration of trajectory for Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) up to the year 2029-30,  
• Setting up of Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Parks to provide land and transmission to RE developers 
for installation of RE projects at large scale,  
• Schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM -KUSUM), 
Solar Rooftop Phase II, 12000 MW CPSU Scheme Phase II, etc, 
• Laying of new transmission lines and creating new sub -station capacity under the Green Energy 
Corridor Scheme for evacuation of renewable power, 
• Notification of standards for deployment of solar photovoltaic system/devices,  
• Setting up of Project Development Cell for attracting and facilitating investments, 
363

• Standard Bidding Guidelines for tariff based competitive bidding process for procurement of Power 
from Grid Connected Solar PV and Wind Projects.  
• Government has issued orders that power shall be dispatched against Letter of Credit (LC) or advance 
payment to ensure timely payment by distribution licensees to RE generators. 
• Notification of Promoting Renewable Energy through Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022. 
• Notification of “The Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and related matters) Rules (LPS rules). 
• Launch of Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) to facilitate sale of Renewable Energy Power through 
exchanges. 
• National Green Hydrogen Mission approved with an aim to make India a global hub for production, 
utilization and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives. 
(c) Ministry of New & Renewable Energy has had consultations with Ministry of Finance regarding 
incentives for implementation of the some of the major schemes such as GEC Phase -II Inter -State 
Transmission System for 13 GW RE in Ladakh, new scheme for Small Hydro Power, and the proposed 
schemes such as Off -grid Solar PV/ Thermal and DRE Livelihood Applications Programme, Offshore 
Wind Power, Renewable Energy Park scheme, etc.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3173 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
RENEWABLE ENERGY PRODUCTION IN THE COUNTRY 
3173. SHRI JOSE K. MANI 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) the percentage of total energy produced in the country through new and renewable energy 
sources; 
(b) the production of new and renewable energy in the country, State-wise and sector-wise; 
(c) whether there is any budgetary allocation by Government to develop the wind energy sector in the 
country; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether Government has been in receipt of any proposal to fully exploit the wind energy 
resources of Western Ghat and coastal areas of Kerala; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b) A total of 1359.97 Billion Units (BU) of electricity have been generated from all sources in 
the country during the year 2022 -23 (up to Jan 2023). Out of which, a total of 316.7 5 BU have been 
generated from renewable energy (RE) which has a share of 23.29% in the total electricity generation 
in the country. 
 
The state-wise details of generation from various RE sources during the current year i.e., 2022-23 (up 
to Jan 2023) are given in Annexure. 
(c) & (d) Wind power projects in the country are set up mostly by private sector developers based on 
techno economic viability of the project at wind potential sites.  
An amount of Rs 1050 crore was allocated for the year 2022 -23 for catering  to committed liabilities 
under wind generation-based Incentive schemes for the wind projects commissioned on or before 31st 
March, 2017. 
Further, an amount of Rs 22 crore was alloc ated in the Budget for the year 2022 -23 for supporting 
research & development activities at National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE). 
(e) & (f) MNRE has not received any  specific proposal to fully exploit the wind energy resources of 
Western Ghat and coastal areas of Kerala.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3174 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
SOLAR WASTE MANAGEMENT 
 
3174. SMT. RANJEET RANJAN 
         SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL 
         DR. AMEE YAJNIK 
 
 
Will the Minister of New and Renewable Energy be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there are measures in place to appropriately discard end-of-life photovoltaic 
hazardous waste, if so, the detail thereof; 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether Government plans on reducing the cost of recycling infrastructure in order to 
incentivise recycling rather than disposal, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
(a) to (d) The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified the E -Waste 
(Management) Rules, 2022 on 2 nd November, 2022. Management of sola r PV modules /panels/ 
cells has been added in Chapter V of the said rules. As per these rules, every manufacturer and 
producer of solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or cells shall: 
 
i. ensure registration on the portal; 
ii. store solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or cells waste generated up to the year 2034 -
35 as per the guidelines laid down by the Central Pollution Control Board in this regard; 
iii. file annual returns in the laid down form on the portal on or before the end of the year to 
which the return relates up to year 2034-35; 
iv. ensure that the processing of the waste other than solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or 
cells shall be done as per the applicable rules or guidelines for the time being in force; 
v. ensure that the inventory  of solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or cells shall be put in 
place distinctly on portal; and 
vi. comply with standard operating procedure and guidelines laid down by the Central 
Pollution Control Board in this regard. 
 
Further, Recycler of solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or cells shall be mandated for recovery 
of material as laid down by the Central Pollution Control Board in this regard. 
MNRE has also called for Research & Development proposals for recycling of solar PV modules.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3175 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
BIOGAS PLANTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH 
3175. SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY 
 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Andhra Pradesh is having second highest biogas plants after 
Madhya Pradesh; 
(b) if so, the details of schemes that the Ministry has to push in setting up more biogas 
plants, particularly in rural Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the details of budget provided for such schemes in 2023-24; 
(d) whether it is a fact that the financial assistance given is not adequate and there have 
been demands for increasing the same; 
(e) if so, the action taken by the Ministry on the above request; and 
(f) the efforts being made to see that one biogas plant is set up in every village of 
Andhra Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER  
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a)  No Sir, State of Maharashtra has the highest number of installed biogas plants followed 
by States of Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh.   
 
(b) The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has notified National Bioenergy 
Programme from year 2021 -22 to 2025 -26. This National Bioenergy Programme has a 
provision for Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for setting up of various capacity of plants 
for generation of biogas (small, medium and large sized plants) in the country under the 
following components: 
(i) Waste to Energy Programme; and  
(ii) Biogas programme 
 
(c) Budgetary outlay of Rs 95.00 Crore has been earmarked under Biogas Programme of 
MNRE for the year 2023-24.  
 
369

(d) & (e) As per the recommendation received from the States, MNRE has increased the 
CFA for setting up the biogas plants in the country.   The details of CFA are given as 
under: 
(i) Rs. 9800/- to Rs. 70,400/- per plant based on size of the plant in cubic meter for 
small biogas plants (1-25 cubic meter/day plant capacity); 
(ii) Rs. 35,000/- to Rs. 45,000/- per kilowatt for power generation and Rs. 17,500 /- to 
Rs. 22,500/- per kilowatt equivalent for thermal applications (25 - 2500 cubic 
meter/day plant capacity);    
In addition to this, there is a provision for 20% higher CFA for special category states 
(North-eastern Region, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir, 
Ladakh, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands) and registered Gaushalas/Shelters. 
 
(f) Towards better adoption of biogas plants in villages, following efforts are, inter alia, 
being made by MNRE: - 
 
(i) Allocation of annual target at the beginning of financial year to States/ Union 
Territories for installing the small biogas plants; 
(ii) Provisions for higher CFA to the biogas beneficiary under categories of Schedule 
Castes / Scheduled Tribes; 
(iii) Additional CFA for linking the biogas plant with slurry filter units and sanitary 
toilet;  
(iv)  Financial support is also being provided for construction, supervision, training for 
biogas skill development, etc;   
(v) For creating awareness about the biogas and its usages among users, biogas 
training programmes are being conducted by the Biogas Development and 
Training Centers at village level; and  
(vi)   For ease of application, Biogas web-portal has been developed for submitting the 
online application by the biogas beneficiary.

available for setting up of community biogas plants in villages, blocks / district. 
(iv) Ministry of Power has notified SAMARTH Mission (National Mission on Use of Biomass 
in Thermal Power Plants) for promoting the blending of biomass in the existi ng coal powered 
thermal power plants.   
(v) Central Pollution Control Board, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has 
notified guidelines to provide financial support for setting up of Biomass Pellet plants in the 
NCT of Delhi, states of Punjab and Haryana and NCR districts of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 3179
ANSWERED ON 28i03/2023
IMPACT OF RESTRAINT ON SHIPS
3I79. SHRI ELAMARAM KAREEM:
will the Minister of PoRTS, sHIpprNG AND wATERwAyS be pleased to srare:
(a) whether Govemment or any competent agency has carried out any study about the impact
and implications likely to be caused in straregic sector of shipping and EXIM Trade because
of immediate restraint on Ships above the age of20 years;
(b) whether any statistics is available with Govemment about number of ship vessels bearing
Indian Flag & Foreign Flags likely to affect operation in the country as a consequence of this
inadvertent change; and
(c) the details of any relief measures being planned for seafarers who are serving onboard
these vessels including their job replacement, being a lockdown like situation in the sector,/
ANSWER
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS
(sHRr SARBANANDA SONOWAL)
(a) to (c) A DGS order No. 06 of 2023 dated 24.02.2023 has been issued by the
Directorate General of Shipping regarding the Age Norms and other eualitative parameters
for registration/ operation of vessels under Indian flag and foreign flagged vessels that are
required to apply for licence under Sections 406 & 407 ofthe Merchant Shipping Act, l95g
(MS Act, 1958), in consultation with the Indian National Ship owners Association (INSA),
other Shipping Agencies and the other stakeholders.
This order prescribes an entry age, qualitative requirements with regard to the
maintenance of the vessel and exit age. However, for Indian flag .Existing vessels'
regardless of its age on the date of issuance of this order, affected by the maximum age
prescribed, has been allowed to operate up to three years from the date ol the issue of
this order in order to give sufficient time for transition.Further, Foreign flagged vessels
requiring licence under Sections 406 &407 of the MS Act l95g and already engaged in
377

-L-
charter on the day of this order, shall also be allowed to operate up to three years from the
date of issue of this Order or until the charter period, whichever is earlier.Thus, the above
provisions under the Order, ensure that there is no immediate restraint on ships above the exit
age already under Indian flag or already operating under existing charter & permitted under
Sections 406 & 407 of MS Act.
The average age ol tndian fleet is higher than that of the world fleet in most of the
vessel categories. Further, in order to achieve the goal under International Maritime
Organization - Sustainable Development Goals embracing technological innovation along
with the transition to low- and zero-carbon fuels and/to altemative energy sources will be
required to achieve these modemization ofthe Indian fleet is pe(inent'
In addition to above, the order dared 24.02.2023 is expected to foster the growth of
quality Indian Tonnage, as the Order creates an entry age criterion for registration. This
would be applicable to foreign flag vessels require<1 to appty for the licence under the Sec 406
& 407 of the MS Act. Hou,ever, an Indian Flag vessel would continue to enjoy the cabotage
after entry age until the prescribed exit age. No foreign flag vessel can compete under the
same age category, thus, creating more demand for Flagging ofvessel under Indian flag.

COASTAL SHIPPING TRAFFIC
3I80. SHRI M. MOHAMEDABDULLA:
Willthe Minister of PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAyS be pleased to stare:
(a) whether there is an increase in the coastal shipping traffic in the last three years and ifso, the
details thereof; and
(b) whether the Union Govemment is going to take any steps to increase the total
freight movement through the water transport in the country and ifso, the details thereofl
ANSWER
MINISTER OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS
(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL)
(a) & (b) Under Sagarmala Programme, various initiatives and projects have been undertaken to
facilitate increase the total freight movement through coastal shipping mode. ln this regard, the
Government has taken following measures to enhance coastal shipping:
(i) Under the Sagarmala Programme, 70 projects worth Rs.2856 crore have been sanctioned
for the development ofCoastal Berths, Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax Jetties/Passenger Jetties etc. Out of
which l5 projects worth Rs. 849 crore have been completed.
(ii) Licensing relaxation under section 407 ofthe Merchant shipping Act is given to container
vessels for carrying EXIM containers and empty containers at transhipment ports for
outbound transport; and to foreign flag vessels carrying agricultural, fisheries,
horticultural, fertilizers and animal produce commodities subject to the condition that
these commodities constitute at least 50% ofthe cargo on board the ship at the beginning
ofthe coastal leg.
(iii) A discount of 4ov" is offered by major ports on vessel and cargo related charges to
coastal cargo vessels.
379

(iu) Priority berthing policy for coastal vessels has been notified to reduce turnaround time
for coastal vessels and improve their utilization.
(v) Reduction of GST on bunker fuels used in Indian Flag Vessels from I 8% to 5%.
(vi) Green channel clearance introduced for faster evacuation of coastal cargo at ports.
(vii) Allowed reimbursement of f'reight subsidy on primary movement of subsidized urea and
P&K fertilizers by coastal shipping or inland water transportation.
(viii) The projects for improvement in the first and last mile road and rail connectivity with all
the major and non-major ports have also been identified for faster cargo movement.
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways is working with Ministry of Railways and
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to implement these projects.

STEPS TO REDUCE INDUSTRIAL EMISSION 
 
3184 SHRI AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH:  
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details regarding industrial emissions by thermal power companies during the last 
five years, year-wise; 
 
(b)  whether it is a fact that the Ministry has sought a two-year extension from the Ministry 
of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for utilities to install emission cutting 
equipment; 
 
(c)  if s o, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  the steps taken to reduce emissions by thermal power companies during the last five 
years? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) 
:  The details regarding Carbon Dioxide (CO 2) emissions by Thermal Power Stations in Metric 
Ton per Mega Watt hour (MWh) generation for the last five years is as follows: 
 
Year CO2 Emission  
(tCO2 /MWh) 
2017-18 0.9598 
2018-19 0.9648 
2019-20 0.9603 
2020-21 0.9493 
2021-22 0.9675 
 
(b) & (c) :  Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the entire process of planning, tendering and 
implementing the Flue Gas De-sulphurisation (FGD) was badly affected. The utilities were facing 
fund constraints and the lenders response had not been encouraging mainly due to poor financial 
conditions of the DISCOMs leading to poor payment position to GENCOs. The geopolitical 
conditions had also affected the import of certain components of FGD which are not manufactured 
in India which has also led to disruption in supply. Therefore, Ministry of Power (MoP) had 
requested Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) on 03.05.2022 to 
provide additional time period of two years to Thermal Power Plants over and above the timelines in  
 
…
…..2.  
385

 
- 2 - 
 
the MoEF&CC Notification dated 31.03.2021, for installation of Flue Gas De-sulphurisation (FGD). 
Subsequently, MoP requested MoEF&CC on 29.07.2022 for phased implementation of FGD in the 
manner (5 Phases upto July 2034), as recommended by IIT Delhi in a study commissioned by MoP 
to assess the compliance of Thermal Power Plants in India to new emission norms.  
 
MoEF&CC vide its Notification dated 05.09.2022 has granted two year extension to the 
timeline for implementation of FGD by TPPs.  
 
(d) 
:  The following steps are taken to reduce emission by Thermal Power Companies during the 
last five years: 
 
i.
 The Thermal Power Stations are required to meet the environmental pollution standard set by 
MoEF&CC from time to time.  
 
ii
. Many TPPs have already adopted use of efficient technologies i.e. from subcritical to 
supercritical and now using ultra-supercritical technology in order to improve efficiency, 
thereby reducing coal consumption and thereby reducing emissions. A total capacity of 
Supercritical and Ultra-supercritical units of 63170 MW (91 supercritical Units) and 1320 
MW (2 ultra supercritical units) have been commissioned till 13.03.2023. 
 
iii. The capacity of about 18362.24 MW comprising 260 units of inefficient and old thermal 
power generation units has already been retired till 31.12.2022.
 
 
iv. Ministry of Power on 08.10.2021 has issued revised policy on Bio-mass Utilization for 
Power Generation through Co-firing in Coal based Power Plants to use 5-10% blend of 
biomass pellets made, primarily of agro-residue alongwith coal after assessing the technical 
feasibility viz. safety aspect,
 etc.   
 
v. Thermal Power Plants of total capacity of about 181 GW is covered under Perform, 
Achieve, Trade (PAT) Scheme and they are given mandatory targets to reduce their specific 
energy consumption i.e. Net Heat Rate (kcal/kwh). 
 
vi. As per revised Nationally Determined Contribution (NDCs) submitted to United Nation 
Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCC) in August, 2022, India’s target is to 
achieve about 50 percent cumulative electric power installed capacity by 2030 from non-
fossil fuel-based energy resources to reduce the Green House Gases (GHGs) emissions.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3187 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
EMPLOYMENT TO LOCAL YOUTH IN NTPC CENTRES 
 
3187 # SMT. GEETA ALIAS CHANDRAPRABHA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of facilities provided to the farmers who have given their land for setting up 
of NTPC centres; 
 
(b)  whether there is a policy to provide employment to the local people in the establishment 
related rules of NTPC centres; 
 
(c)  if so, the number of local people who were provided employment in the NTPC centres 
located in Auraiya district of Uttar Pradesh so far, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)  whether any special arrangement has been made for the education of local people in 
Kendriya Vidyalaya being operated at NTPC campus, Auraiya, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) 
:   The land for NTPC Projects has been/is acquired by the respective State Government/ 
District Administration under the extant Land Acquisition Act. The compensation for the acquisition 
of various land parcels & assets of the farmers is decided & declared by the State 
Governments/District Administration under the extant Land Acquisition Act. 
 
As far as the Rehabilitation and Re-settlement (R&R) of the Project Affected Persons is 
concerned, NTPC acts as per the provisions of the extant NTPC R&R Policy, Government 
Guidelines/extant Land Acquisition Act.  
 
Individual R&R benefits to the eligible project affected persons are also extended by way of 
area development through execution of various community development activities, education and 
health facilities. Further, petty works, through PAPs (Project Affected Persons) cooperative 
societies, like hiring of vehicles, allotment of shops etc. have been extended to the PAPs and their 
families at various stations/projects of NTPC. 
 
NTPC under its CSR Policy is also working in the fields of health, education, sanitation, skill 
development,
 etc. for the development of the surrounding areas including the project affected 
villages. 
………2. 
 
399

- 2 - 
(b):   NTPC projects are developed with the State-of-the-Art technology; so direct job 
opportunities are severely restricted. However, NTPC gives preference to the affected families in 
providing employment in the project, subject to the availability of vacancies and suitability of the 
affected person for employment.  
As per NTPC R&R policies so far and Government guidelines, preference to PAPs in 
permanent employment subject to the availability of vacancies, required skill-sets for the job and 
suitability of the PAPs (Project Affected Persons) was given. However, secondary employment 
opportunities to the project affected persons with the contracting agencies, as also economic 
opportunities such as hiring of vehicles, allotment of shops, award of petty contracts to the PAP Co-
operatives, etc. are also extended to the PAPs. 
 
(c) 
:   NTPC Auraiya has provided permanent employment to 49 land oustees of project affected 
villages as per the extant policy and rules of the Company. Along with this, from time to time, 
NTPC Auraiya awarded contract to land oustees & hired vehicles on contract basis from the Project 
Affected Families.  
According to the Contractor's Labor Information Management System (CLIMS) records 
implemented in NTPC Auraiya, presently 329 contract workers are working in various agencies from 
PAP family & local villages. 
 
(d) 
:   A Kendriya Vidyalaya at NTPC Auraiya’s Township-Dibiyapur was established for 
imparting quality education to the wards of NTPC employees, C.I.S.F employees and the adjoining 
population, subject to availability of seats in respective classes and admission guidelines. All the 
basic necessary facilities for the normal operation of this School have been provided by NTPC. 
The admissions are given by the School Management,  as per the Kendriya Vidyalaya 
Sangthan Policy and Rules. Admission is imparted against the available seats, giving due priority to 
the wards of employees of Central Government/PSUs/ Defense/ Ex-Servicemen/ State Government, 
etc. As of now, 235 students/wards of Government Public Sector Undertakings, Government 
Employees, State Government etc. and local people are studying in this School.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3189 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
ELECTRICITY FROM GAS PLANTS 
 
3189 # SHRI NARAIN DASS GUPTA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the total number of gas plants at present along with their location from which electricity is 
being generated in the country; 
 
(b)  whether some of the gas plants are closed down; 
 
(c)  if so, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d)  whether Government is considering to restart these closed gas plants; and 
 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a):    The Central Electricity Authority under Ministry of Power, monitors 62 gas based power 
stations, with a total capacity of 23,845 MW using gas as primary fuel. The list of gas based  power 
plants, along with their location, is attached at Annexure.  
 
The requirement of gas for these power plants at 90% Plant Load Factor (PLF) is 115 Million 
Metric Standard Cubic Meters per day (MMSCMD). During the year 2022-23 (April, 2022 to 
January, 2023), the total gas available
 to power sector was only about 16.14 MMSCMD,  comprising 
of 13.21 MMSCMD domestic gas and 2.93 MMSCMD imported Re-gasified Liquefied Natural Gas 
(RLNG). 
 
 
(b) & (c) :  During 2022-23 (April, 2022 to January, 2023), the gas based capacity of 9308 MW (28 
gas based plants) had NIL generation and the overall Plant Load Factor (PLF) of gas-based power 
plants remained only around 12% due to less availability of domestic gas and high price of imported 
RLNG.  
 
 
(d) & (e):  In order to meet the projected peak demand of around 230 GW during April – May, 
2023, the Government of India approved a mechanism for operationalization of around 5000 MW 
NTPC gas based capacity during this period. Further, the Government has also planned for additional 
procurement of power from gas based capacity (other than NTPC Plants) during this period.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3190 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
POWER PROJECTS IN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
3190 # SMT. KANTA KARDAM: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the number of power projects running in Uttar Pradesh, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  the funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized under these projects during the last two 
years, the present status of these projects; 
 
(c)  whether some of these projects are facing huge cost/time overrun and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
 
(d)  the action taken/being taken by Government for timely completion of these projects?  
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) :    Presently, five power projects are under construction in the State of Uttar Pradesh. T he 
details of funds sanctioned, allocated & utilized along with their present status are given at 
Annexure.
 
 The following steps have been taken by the Government to ensure timely completion of 
Power Projects: - 
(i) The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) monitors the progress of under construction power projects 
through periodic review meetings, site visits and interaction with the developers & other stakeholders 
to identify and resolve issues critical for commissioning of Projects.

facilitate faster resolution of inter-ministerial and other outstanding issues. 
(iii) In case of Central Power Sector Undertakings (CPSU’s) projects, the project implementation

STATUS OF ONGOING POWER PROJECTS IN TAMIL NADU 
 
3191  SHRI K.R.N. RAJESHKUMAR:  
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of the ongoing power projects in Tamil Nadu; 
 
(b)  the funds sanctioned, allocated and utilized under these projects during the last five years; 
 
(c)  whether some of these projects are facing huge cost/time overrun and if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d)  the action taken by Government for timely completion of these projects? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) 
: The ongoing Power Projects in the State of Tamil Nadu are given below: 
 
(i) North Chennai Thermal Power Project, Stage-III (1x800 MW) 
(ii) Ennore SEZ Thermal power Project (2x660 MW) 
(iii) Udangudi STPP, Stage-I (2x660 MW) 
(iv) Ennore Exp Thermal power Project (1x660 MW) 
(v) Kundah Pump Storage Project (4x125 MW)  
(vi) Kollimalai Hydro Electric Project (1x20 MW)  
 
(b) & (c) :  The details are enclosed at Annexure. 
 
(d) :  Government of India has taken various measures for timely completion of projects, 
which are as under: 
 
(i) The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) monitors the progress of under construction 
power projects through periodic review meetings, site visits and interaction with the 
developers & other stakeholders to identify and resolve issues critical for commissioning 
of projects. 
 
(ii) Regular reviews are also undertaken by the Ministry of Power (MoP) to identify the 
constraints and facilitate faster resolution of Inter-Ministerial and other outstanding 
issues. 
 
(iii) In case of Central Power Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) projects, the project 
Implementation parameters / milestones are incorporated in the annual MoU signed 
between respective CPSU and MoP and the same are monitored during the Quarterly 
Performance Review (QPR) meetings of CPSUs and other meetings held in MoP/ CEA. 
 
(iv) Various matters related with project implementation are being taken up with State 
Government/District Administration for expeditious resolution of issues.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3192 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28TH MARCH, 2023 
 
HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE COUNTRY 
 
 
3192 SHRI ABDUL WAHAB: 
 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact the there is a shortage of Primary Health Clinics (PMCs) in many districts 
of the country; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether Government has any data on the number of Primary Health Clinics; 
(d) the details of Government hospitals and medical colleges established by Government in the 
last five years, State wise, district wise and year wise; and 
(e) the number of doct ors currently working at Primary Health Clinics and Government 
hospitals? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE 
(DR. BHARATI PRAVIN PAWAR) 
 
(a) to (d) :  As per the norms under Indian Public Health Standards(IPHS) 2022, a PHC in rural area 
can be established for a population of 30,000 in plains and 20,000 in hilly and tribal areas. Urban 
PHCs can be established at a population of 50,000.  
Rural Health Statistics (RHS) is an annual publication, based on Health care administrative 
data reported by States/UTs. As per RHS 2021 -22, State/UT-wise details of PHCs may be seen at 
the following link of RHS 2021-22: 
https://main.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/RHS%202021%2022.pdf 
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the 
States/UTs to strengthen the public healthcare system, based on the proposals received in the form 
of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission.  Government of India 
provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proc eedings (RoPs) as per norms & 
available resources.  
412

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for ‘Establishment of new Medical Colleges 
attached with existing district/referral hospitals’, a total of 157 medical colleges have been 
sanctioned in three phases with fund sharing between the Centre and State Governments in the ratio 
of 90:10 for North eastern and Special Category States and 60:40 for others. Out of these, 104 
colleges have been approved in last five years i.e. from 2017 -18 to 2021 -22.  Details  are at 
Annexure-I.  
Further, under PMSSY Nine new AIIMS for establishment and two Government Medical 
Colleges/Institutions (GMCIs) for upgradation  have been approved  during last 5 years, details are at 
Annexure-II.  
 
 Progress over the year, in respect o f details of Sub Divisional Hospitals, District Hospitals 
and Medical Colleges established by state Government in the last five years, State wise, district 
wise and year wise can be accessed through comparing RHS 2021-22 from 2016-17.  
RHS 2016-17 can be seen through following link: 
 
https://main.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/RHS%201516%2017.pdf 
  
(e) Details of doctors currently working at Primary Health Centre, Sub-District hospitals and 
District hospitals may also be seen  through link of RHS 2021-22.

THE ELECTRICITY (AMENDMENT) BILL 
 
3193  SMT. JEBI MATHER HISHAM: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether robust provisions have been incorporated in The Electricity (Amendment) Bill to 
ensure the financial stability of the farmers and food security for the nation, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b)  the provision which have been incorporated in the Bill regarding subsidies, taking into 
account the interest of consumers, especially household consumers and farmers, the 
details thereof; and 
 
(c)  whether Government will provide the data on the subsidies given to household 
consumers and farmers, if so, the details over the last five years, State-wise?

E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b)  :  The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 covers amendment s related to power sector. 
There is no amendment proposal related to agriculture sector in the Electricity  (Am endment) Bill, 
2022. Further, the provision of subsidy as in the present Act i.e. Electricity Act, 2003 is not proposed 
to be changed and the State Governments can continue to give subsidy to farmers  and other 
consumers as they are doing at present.

3194 #  SHRI BRIJLAL: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER

BIMSTEC Energy Center (BEC) in Bengaluru and if so, the details thereof and the outcome 
of the said meeting;

recommendations made in the meeting regarding the present energy scenario in the 
BIMSTEC region; and 
 
(c)  whether any agreement was signed between Government of India and the BIMSTEC in 
the field of energy cooperation and if so, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) : Yes, Sir .  India hosted the first meeting of the Governing Board of the Bay of Bengal 
Initiative for Multi -Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Energy Cent er in 
Bengaluru on 27.02.2023. The outcome of the Meeting are as under:- 
 
i. Additional Secreta ry, Ministry of Power, has been nominated as the Member of 
Governing Board of the BIMSTEC Energy Center (BEC)  from India. 
 
ii. Chairperson CEA, Ministry of Power, Govt. of India, has been appointed as the first 
Executive Director of the BIMSTEC Energy Center from India.

(b) : The delegations from Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand, 
participated in the Meeting.  
  
 The present energy scenario was discussed by the delegates from the respective countries of

(c) :  No specific agreement was signed between Government of India and the BIMSTEC in 
the field of energy cooperation in the first Meeting of the Governing Board of the BEC.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3196 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
STEPS TO MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF DISASTERS 
 
3196  SMT. MAMATA MOHANTA: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government has been assessing the severe damages in disasters like cyclones, super-
cyclones in various part of the country particularly in the coastal States like Odisha; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the assessmen t made by Government; 
 
(c)  the steps being taken by the Ministry to mitigate the impact of disasters like cyclones ranging 
from severe to extremely severe in intensity and floods which badly affects various 
districts of Odisha; and 
 
(d)  whether Government has chalked out any robust plan to deal with such issues? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b) :  The primary responsibility for disaster management rests with the State Government. 
As such, the concerned State Governments are responsible for undertaking damage assessment in the 
area affected by notified natural calamities including cyclone. Financial assistance from the State 
Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) is provided to the 
State as per established procedure. 
 
However, as per revised items & norms, assistance is provided limited to immediate 
restoration of electricity supply in the affected areas for the damaged conductor, poles and 
transformers upto 11 kV. 
 
(c) & (d) : The measures taken by the Central and State Governments have significantly improved 
the disaster management practices, preparedness, prevention and response mechanisms resulting in 
significant reduction in casualties during natural calamities, including cyclones, in the country. 
Further, strengthening of the disaster management is a continuing and evolving process of 
governance. 
 
Some of the measures being taken to mitigate the impact of Disasters and ensure 
uninterrupted power supply are as under: 
 
(i) Additional financial assistance is provided to States from Nation Disaster Response Fund 
(NDRF), as per laid down procedure is case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which includes 
as assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). 
 
…….2.
 
 
424

- 2 - 
 
(ii) Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has issued Disaster Management Plan, 2022 . It 
provides a framework and direction to the utilities in the Power Sector for all phases of 
the disaster management cycle (i.e. Mitigation, Preparedness, Response and Recovery). 
 
(iii) CEA has notified the Central Electricity Authority (Technical Standards for Construction 
of Electrical Plants and Electric Lines) Regulations, 2022 on 23.12.2022 wherein several 
provisions regarding disaster mitigation were introduced. 
 
(iv) Inter-State and Inter-Regional Power Transfer by strengthening of inter-regional 
transmission links and formation of National Grid. 
 
(v
) Strengthening / Augmentation of sub-transmission and distribution systems- Under the 
RDSS Scheme launched by Government of India in July,
 2021 financial assistance is 
being provided for works like underground cabling,  etc, specified in the Disaster 
Management Plan for Power Sector issued by Central Electricity Authority in January,  
2021 and its future amendments, if any and the Disaster Resilient Works specified by 
National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). 
 
(vi) Strict monitoring to ensure timely completion of ongoing / sanctioned projects.

REQUIREMENT, DEMAND AND SUPPLY OF ELECTRICITY 
 
3197 #  SHRI SATISH CHANDRA DUBEY: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether Government has done any assessment of electricity requirement, demand and supply 
in both peak and non-peak hours, for the next five years, State-wise; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof including potential capacity growth, State/UT- wise; and 
 
(c)  the necessary steps being taken to meet the demand of electricity and the amount being 
invested in it? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) & (b) : The 20th Electric Power Survey (EPS) Report, published by Central Electricity Authority 
(CEA) in November 2022, covers electricity demand projection for the year 2021-22 to 2031-32 as 
well as perspective electricity demand projection for the year 2036-37 and 2041-42 for the country. 
 
       
 The estimated energy requirement and peak demand of the country State/UT-wise from the 
year 2022-23 to 2026-27 is given at Annexure. 
 
(c) :  The steps taken/being taken by the Government to meet the demand of electricity and 
investment in it are as follows: 
 
(i) In order to meet the growing demand of electricity, there is need for fresh generation capacity 
addition. As per draft National Electricity Plan for the period 2022-27 which is under 
approval, an investment of about Rs.14.54 lakh crore would be required to install additional 
generation capacity 
of about 210 GW during 2022-27 along with battery storage of 
8680MW/ 34720 MWh. 
 
(ii) Thermal Power Plants of 25,440 MW of capacity are at various stages of construction in the 
country.  
 
(iii) Hydroelectric projects (above 25 MW) totaling to 17803.5 MW are under implementation. 
 
(iv) Nuclear Power Plants of 8,700 MW of capacity are under construction and 7000 MW of 
Nuclear power plants have been accorded Sanction. 
 
……..2. 
 
 
426

- 2 - 
 
(v) The capacity of National Grid is being expanded on a continuous basis commensurate with 
the growth in electricity generation and electricity demand. It is planned to add about 17,500 
ckm of transmission lines and 80,000 MVA of transformation capacity per year (220 kV and 
above voltage level) on all India basis. The present inter-regional capacity of the National 
Grid is 1,1
2,250 MW and is likely to go upto about 1,50,000 MW by 2030. 
 
(vi) Government has set a target to achieve 50 percent cumulative electric power installed 
capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources by 2030. As of February,
 2023, India's 
total utility scale installed solar capacity is around 64.4 GW. As on February,  2023, India's 
total installed wind capacity is around 42 GW. As on February,  2023, total installed non-
fossil based capacity is around 176 GW out of total capacity of 412 GW. The likely installed 
capacity of non-fossil fuel of the country by the end of year 2029-30 will be around 500 GW.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3199 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
LIFTING OF COAL FOR POWER REQUIREMENTS 
 
3199  SHRI JAVED ALI KHAN:  
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Ministry vide communication dated 30.11.2022 has written to State 
Government of Punjab to lift coal for power requirements from Mahanadi and Talchar 
coalfields in Odisha through Rail Ship Rail (RSR) mode/route from January 2023; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the detailed route; 
 
(c)  the response of Punjab Government thereto; and 
 
(d)  the details of other States which have been advised to shift to this RSR route?  
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) : Due to steep increase in energy demand and constrained supply of domestic coal, various 
Central/ State Gencos and IPPs import coal for blending with  domestic coal in their Thermal Power 
Plants. With a view to reduce import of coal for blending purposes being costlier, as well as to ease 
out the logistics pressure on Railways in evacuating coal from Mahanadi Coalfield Limited (MCL) 
region, Ministry of Power,
 vide letter dated 30.11.2022, advised the States of Punjab, Rajasthan, 
Gujarat, Maharashtra and NTPC to transport part of their total domestic coal requirements using 
Rail-Ship-Rail (RSR) route. 
 
In response to State of Punjab Government’s letter dated 08.12.2022, Ministry of Power vide 
letter dated 24.02.2023 has informed that as extra coal is only available in the MCL and evacuation 
of this additional coal from MCL is only possible through Port of Paradip as the All Rail Route is 
congested, so Punjab State and Western States were asked to take coal from the sea route from 
Paradip Port to their generating stations.  If,
 the State of Punjab does not want to do so, it is the 
choice of Punjab State.    
 
Government of India does not mandate any particular route or Port and coal transport is 
entirely the decision of the concerned States/Generators. 
 
The Rail-Ship-Rail route for transport of coal from MCL would be Rail from MCL to 
Eastern Ports, Eastern Ports to Western Ports by coastal shipping and Western Ports to the power 
plants located in the Northern and Western parts of the country by rail route.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF POWER

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3200 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2023 
 
SMART METERS 
 
3200 # MS. INDU BALA GOSWAMI: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a)  the amount of financial assistance that has been approved by the Union Government for the 
project of installation of smart meters in Himachal Pradesh; 
 
(b)  whether there is a proposal to recharge on the lines of mobiles for electricity facility in 
future; and 
 
(c)  if so, the details thereof? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF POWER 
AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY  
 
(SHRI R.K. SINGH) 
 
(a) 
:   Financial assistance for Prepaid Smart Metering & System Metering is envisaged under the 
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS). Under RDSS,  Rs. 1788.49 crore (including Project 
Monitoring Agency, PMA charges) with a GBS of Rs . 466.23 crore (including PMA charges)  have 
been sanctioned by the Government of India for installation of 28,00,945 No. of Smart P re-paid 
Consumer Meters, 39,012 N o. of Smart DT Meters and 1,951 No. of Smart Feeder Meters in the 
State of Himachal Pradesh. 
 
(b) & (c) :  Under RDSS, the installation of Smart Meters is being taken up in pre-paid mode, across 
the country. The Smart Meters would be connected to Meter Data Management (MDM) system 
through communication media which facilitates the recharge of Smart Meter through various 
mediums on the line of mobiles. Smart Meters can be recharged through mobile app, consumer 
portal, on-line banking, credit cards payment, wallets, etc. The consumer portal/application will als o 
enable consumers to recharge as well as view recharge history, existing balance, daily usage,
 etc.

वषच प्रवत पररवार 5 लाख रु . तक का स्वास््य बीमा प्रदाभ ककया जाता है। एबी-पीएमजेएवाई क े  तहत 
सवममवलत पररवारों की सं्या का राज्य/संघ राज्य क्षेत्रवार ब्यौरा अभुलग्नक-I में कदया गया है। सामावजक 
आर्थचक जावतगत जभगणभा (एसईसीसी), 2011 क े  डाटाबेस क े  अभुसार, इस स्कीम में 8.19 करो ड ग्रामीण 
पररवारों को िावमल ककया गया है। राज्यों /संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों को छूट दी गई है कक वे िेष रह गए  
(अप्रमावणत) एसईसीसी पररवारों को भामांककत करभे क े  वलए गैर -एसईसीसी लाभाथी पररवार डाटाबेस 
का प्रयोग करें। तदभुसार, अभेक राज्यों/संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों भे अवर्वनभत एसईसीसी पररवारों और ववस्ताररत 
लाभाथी आधार क े सापेक्ष वभधचभ और कमजोर पररवारों क े  डाटाबेस को साझा ककया है। इभ डाटाबेसों को 
काडच बभाभे क े  वलए एभएर्ए की सूर्भा प्रौद्योवगकी प्रणाली क े  साथ एकीक ृत  ककया गया है।  
देि में भारतीय बीमा वववभयामक और ववकास प्रावधकरण (आईआरडीएआई ) में पंजीक ृ त बीमाकताचओं 
द्वारा वव् वषच 2021-22 में स्वास््य बीमा क े  अंतगचत कवर ककए गए व्यवियों की सं्या का राज्य/संघ 
राज्य क्षेत्रवार ब्यौरा अभुलग्नक-II में कदया गया है। एभएसओ की ररपोटों क े अभुसार , ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में 
लगभग 14.1% लोगों क े  पास स्वास््य बीमा है। वषच 2021-22 क े  दौराभ जीवभ बीमाकताचओं द्वारा जारी 
की गई स्वास््य बीमा पॉवलवसयों का बीमाकताच -वार ब्यौरा अभुलग्नक-III में कदया गया है।  वषच 2021-22 
क े  दौराभ ग्रामीण क्षेत्र में सामान्य और स्टैंड एलोभ स्वास््य बीमाकताचओं द्वारा जारी की गई स्वास््य बीमा 
पॉवलवसयों का बीमाकताच -वार ब्यौरा अभुलग्नक-IV में कदया गया है।  
देि में स्वास््य बीमा की पहंर् बढाभे में सहायता संबंधी पहलें आईआरडीएआई द्वारा की जाती हैं। 
बीमाकताचओं को सलाह दी जाती है कक वे वव्ीय सुरक्षा क े  तंत्र क े  रूप में बीमा की आवश्यकता क े  बारे में 
जागरुकता बढाएं।

 क्मा यसामन औय उववयक  भंत्री मह फताने की कृऩा कयेंगे कक :

लनमावत ककए जाने वारे कप लसयऩ भें ववषैरे तत्व ऩाए जाने संफंधी रयऩोर्व का संऻान 
लरमा है ;  
(ख) क्मा सयकाय इसभें शालभर बायतीम कंऩलनमों क े  ववलनभावण संफंधी भानकों की जांर् शुरू 
कयने का इयादा यखती है ; 
(ग) क्मा सयकाय को उक्त कप लसयऩ क े  बायतीम फाजायों भें प्रर्रन का ऩता र्रा है ; 
औय 
(घ) क्मा सयकाय इसभें शालभर बायतीम कंऩलनमों द्वाया लनलभवत औय लनमावत ककए जाने वारे 
कप लसयऩ क े  संफंध भें वैम्िक र्ेतावनी जायी कयने का इयादा यखती है?

कदनांक 28.03.2023 को उत्तय देने क े  लरए तायांककत प्रश्न सं्‍मा 287 क े  बाग (क) से (घ) क े  
उत्तय भें उम्लरम्खत वववयण 
(क) औय (ख): ववषम वस्तु स्वास््म औय ऩरयवाय कलमाण ववबाग से संफंलधत है। गाम्बफमा भें 
रयऩोर्व की गई भौतों क े  भाभरे भें, भैससव भेडेन पाभावस्मूकर्कलस लरलभर्ेड 81, एर्एसआईडीसी 
औद्योलगक ऺेत्र, क ुंडरी-131028, म्जरा सोनीऩत (हरयमाणा) भें याज्म औषलध लनमंत्रक, हरयमाणा क े  
सभन्वम भें सीडीएससीओ द्वाया एक संमुक्त जांर् की गई औय दवाइमों क े  लनमंत्रण नभूने लरए गए 
औय ऺेत्रीम औषलध ऩयीऺण प्रमोगशारा, (आयडीर्ीएर) र्ंडीगढ़ को ऩयीऺण औय ववश्लेषण क े  लरए 
बेजे गए। आयडीर्ीएर र्ंडीगढ़ क े  सयकायी ववश्लेषक की रयऩोर्व क े  अनुसाय, नभूने भानक गुणवत्ता वारे 
घोवषत ककए गए थे। उक्त नभूने डामलथरीन ग्राइकॉर (डीईजी) औय एलथरीन ग्राइकॉर (ईजी) दोनों 
क े  लरए बी नकायात्भक ऩाए गए थे। 
 
मद्यवऩ, अच्छी ववलनभावण ऩम्ततमों भें ऩाए गए उलरंघनों क े  आधाय ऩय, याज्म औषलध लनमंत्रक, 
हरयमाणा ने कदनांक 7.10.2022 को भैससव भेडेन पाभाव को कायण फताओ नोकर्स जायी ककमा। इसक े  
अलतरयक्त, भैससव भेडेन पाभावस्मुकर्कलस लरलभर्ेड, सोनीऩत, हरयमाणा को कदनांक 11.10.2022 को

(क ) से (ग): भारत सरकार गभचवती माताओं और तभके बच्चों् के स्वास््य और आरोग् य को सिवभवित करभे के 
वलए राष्ट्रीय स्वास््य वमशभ के तहत वववभन्न स्कीमें कायाचवववत करती है, वजसमें कामकाजी माताओं के पांर् 
वर्च से कम आयि के बच्चों् को भी कवर ककया जाता है। इभ योजभाओं में वभम् भवलवखत शावमल हैं: 
1. जभभी सिरा ा योजभा (जेएसवाई ), एक मांग संव चभ और सशतच भकि हस्तांतरण योजभा है वजसका तद्देश्य 
संस्थागत प्रसव को बढावा िेभा है। जेएसवाई के छंतगचत वव्ीय सहायता तभ राज्यों्/संघ राज्य ा ेत्रों् में 
सभी   गभचवती मवहलाओं को तपलय  है वजवहें वभम्न कायच वभष् पािभ वाले राज्यों् के रूप में वगीकृत ककया गया 
है। तथावप, शेर् राज्यों्/संघ राज्य ा ेत्रों् में जहां संस्थागत प्रसव के स्तर संतोर्जभक हैं (तच्च कायच वभष्पािभ वाले 
राज्यों् के रूप में वगीकृत ), केवल गरीबी रेखा से भीर्े  जीवभ  यापभ करभे वाले पररवार /छभिसूवर्त 
जावत /छभिसूवर्त जभजावत पररवारों् की गभचवती मवहलाएं ही जभभी सिरा ा योजभा के लाभों् की हकिार हैं। गृह 
प्रसव के वलए , जेएसवाई के तहत वव्ीय सहायता केवल बीपीएल पररवारों् की गभचवती मवहलाओं के वलए 
तपलय  है।  
2. जभभी वशशि सिरा ा कायचक्रम (जेएसएसके ) प्रतयेक गभचवती मवहला को वभ:शिल् क पररवहभ , वभिाभ, िवाओं , 
छवय तपभोग्य सामवियों्, आहार और रक्त (यकि आवश्यक हो) के प्राव ाभ के साथ-साथ जभ स्वास््य संस्थाभों् 
में सीजेररयभ सेक्शभ सवहत वभ:शिल् क प्रसव का  हक प्रिाभ करता है। तपर्ार के वलए जभ स्वास््य संस्थाभ आभे 
वाले सभी बीमार वशशिओं के वलए समाभ पात्रताएं छव कार  मचजूि हैं। 
3. प्र ाभमंत्री सिरवा त मातृतव छवभयाभ (पीएमएसएमए) हर महीभे की 9 तारीख को सभी गभचवती मवहलाओं 
को तभके िूसरी  /तीसरी  वतमाही में सावचभचवमक रूप से वभवित, सिवभवित, व्यापक और गिणव्ापूणच प्रसवपूवच 
पररर्याच प्रिाभ करता है। छवभयाभ के भाग के रूप में सरकारी स्वास््य सिवव ा केव रों् में ओबीजीवाई 
ववशेर्ज्ञों्/रेवडयोलॉवजस्ट/वर्ककतसा छव काररयों् द्वारा प्रसवपूवच पररर्याच सेवाओं का वयूभतम पैकेज प्रिाभ 
ककया जाता है।   
4. प्रसव का  गिणवत ता सि ार पहल (लक्ष्य) का तद्देश्य प्रसव का  और मैटरवभटी ऑपरेशभ वथएटरों् में पररर्याच

और प्रसव के तिरंत बाि सम्माभजभक और गिणव्ापूणच पररर्याच प्राप्त हो। 
5. सिरवा त मातृतव आश्वासभ (सिमभ) का तद्देश्य वबभा ककसी लागत के सिवभवित, आश् वावसत , सम्माभजभक 
और गिणव्ापूणच स्वास््य पररर्याच सेवा प्रिाभ करभा है और जभ स्वास््य सिवव ा केव रों् पर आभे वाली प्रतयेक 
मवहला और भवजात वशशि के वलए सेवाओं से इभकार के वलए शूवय सवहष्णिता है। 
6. सिवव ा केव र आ ाररत भवजात पररर्याच: रूग् ण भवजात पररर्याच इकाइयां (एसएभसीयू) वजला छस्पताल 
और मेवडकल कॉलेज स्तर पर स्थावपत की जाती हैं, भवजात वस्थरीकरण इकाइयां (एभबीएसयू) बीमार और

छोटे बच्चों् की िेखभाल के वलए प्रथम रेफरल इकाइयों् (एफआरयू)/सामििावयक स्वास््य केंरों् (सीएर्सी) में 
स्थावपत की जाती हैं।

8. मॉं का छसीम स्नेह (एमएए): मॉं का छसीम स्नेह (एमएए) के तहत पहले छह महीभों् के वलए शिरूआती पहल

9. वभमोवभया को बेछसर करभे के वलए सामावजक जागरूकता और कारचवाई (एसएएएभएस) पहल वर्च 2019

10. राष्ट्रीय बाल स्वास््य कायचक्रम (आरबीएसके ): बाल तत तरजीववता  में सि ार के वलए राष्ट्रीय बाल स्वास््य 
कायचक्रम (आरबीएसके ) के तहत 0 से 18 वर्च तक के बच्चों् की 32 स्वास््य संबं ी वस्थवतयों् (छथाचत् रोग , 
खावमयों्, िोर्ों् और ववकासातमक ववलम् ब) के वलए जांर् की जाती है। आरबीएसके के छंतगचत जांर् ककए गए 
बच्चों् की पिवि और प्रबं भ के वलए वजला स्वास््य सिवव ा केव रों् के स्तर पर वजला प्रारंवभक कायचकलाप केंर 
(डीईआईसी) स्थावपत ककए जाते हैं।

(ि)‍ से‍(ग): विनांक  31. 12.2022 की वथिवत क े  अनुसार सकल अनिचक आवथतयों (एनपीए) का

क्षेत्र क े  बैंकों (पीएसबी) द्वारा बट्टे खाते डाले गए ऋणों का बैंक-िार ब्यौरा अनुबंध-2 में विया गया है। 
भारतीय ररज़िच बैंक (आरबीआई) क े  विशावनिेशों और बैंक क े  बोडच द्वारा अनुमोवित नीवत क े  अनुसार 
एनपीए, विसमें िैसे एनपीए भी शावमल हैं , विनक े  र्ार िर्च पूरा होने पर पूणच प्रािधान वकया गया है, को 
बट्टे खाते डालकर संबंवधत बैंक क े  तुलन पत्र से हटा विया िाता है। आरबीआई क े  विशावनिेशों और 
बैंक क े  बोडच द्वारा अनुमोवित नीवतयों क े  अनुसार बैंक अपने तुलन पत्र को पररशुद्ध करने, कर लाभ प्राप् त 
करने और पूंिी को इष्टतम बनाने क े  वलए अपने वनयवमत कायच क े  रूप में बट्टे खाते डाले िाने क े  प्रभाि 
का म ूलयांकन करते हैं /उन पर विर्ार करते हैं। इस प्रकार बट्टे खाते डाले िाने से उधारकताचओं को 
पुनभुचगतान क े  िावयत्ि से छू ट नहीं वमलती है। र्ूूँवक बट्टे खाते डाले गए ऋणों क े  उधारकताच पुनभुचगतान क े

भारत सरकार

स्वास््य और पररवार कल्याण ववभाग 
 
राज् य सभा 
तारांककत प्रश् भ सं्या: *298 
किभांक  28 मार्च, 2023 को पूछे जाभे वाले प्रश् भ का त्र  
 
स् वास् ् य क्षेत्र में रोवगयों द्वारा वहभ ककया जाभे वाला व् यय 
 
*298.  डॉ. अमर पटभायक : 
  
क्या स् वास् ् य और पररवार कल् याण मंत्र   यह बताभे की कृपा करेंगे कक : 
 
(क ): वर्च 2020 से वर्च 2023 तक समग्र स् वास् ् य व् यय में मात्रा की िृवि से केन्द् ् सरकार की कहल वहस् से िार  
और कहल स् वास् ् य व् यय में तसकी प्रवतततता का वर्च -वार ब यौ‍रा क् या है ; 
(ख): वर्च 2020 से वर्च 2023 तक स् वास् ् य पर मात्रा की िृवि से रोवगयों द्वारा वहभ ककए जाभे वाले व् यय की 
कहल वहस् सेिार  और कहल स् वास् ् य व् यय में तसकी प्रवतततता का वर्च-वार ब यौ‍रा क् या है; 
(ग): क् या यह सर् है कक स् वा स् ् य पर रोवगयों द्वारा वहभ ककया जाभे वाला व् य य वभरंतर अवकक रहा है  और 
इसकी िर बहुत अवकक अर्ाचत् 48.2 प्रवततत रह  है ; और  
(घ): यकि हां , तो सरकार द्वारा रोवगयों द्वारा वहभ ककए जाभे वाले व् यय को कम करभे के वलए क् या  किम तएाए 
गए हैं  ?

स् वास् ् य और पररवार कल् या ण मंत्र  (डॉ. मभसहख मांडववया) 
 
 
(क ) से (घ): वववरण सिभ के पटल पर रख किया गया है।

3042. श्री नरहरी अमीन:  
 
क्या आयुष मंत्री यह बताने की क ृ पा करेंगे ककिः  
 
(क ) क् या शेम में आय ुष चर्ककत सा पधति त को ब ढ़वा शेने क े  ललए चर्ककत सा  संबंिी षवषयप पर आिातरत 
सवेक्षण कराने की कोई योजना बनाई गई है ; 
(ख ) यदश हां , तो क् या शेम में सव ेक्षण क े  आिार पर आय ुष चर्ककत सा  पधति त पर आिातरत नी त पर 
षवर्ार ककया जाएगा ; और  
(ग)   ककन प्रम ुख बबंश ुओं पर सव ेक्षण ककया जा रहा है , तत सं बंिी य यर रा क् या है ? 
 
उत्तर 
आमुोयमांत्रवय(श्रवयसधाानांदयसोणोयाल) 
 
(क ) से (ग): जुलाई , 2022 माह में सांख्ययकी एवं कायचक्रम कायाचन्वयन मंत्रालय (एमओएसपीआई ) धतवारा 
आय ुष पर एक सव ेक्षण मुरू ककया गया है और वतचमान में सवेक्षण क े  ललए डेटा संग्रह का कायच प्रग त पर 
है। आय ुष मंत्रालय साक्ष्यप और आंकडप क े  आिार पर षवलभन्न नी तयां बनाता है।   
 
आय ुष से संबंचित  नम्नललखखत व्यापक क्षेत्रप पर जानकारी एकत्र करने क े  ललए सव ेक्षण तैयार ककया गया 
है:- 
 
(i) आय ुष चर्ककतसा पधति तयप  क े  बारे में जागरूकता।   
(ii) संशभाचिीन अवचि में पतरवारप धतवारा आय ुष चर्ककतसा पधति तयप का उपयोग।  
(iii) अस्पताल में भती और अस्पताल क े  बाहर  इलाज क े  ललए आय ुष चर्ककतसा पधति त यप  का उपयोग।  
(iv) प्रसव पूवच और प्रसवोत्तर शेखभाल क े  ललए आय ुष चर्ककतसा पधति तयप का उपयोग।   
(v) आय ुष शवाओं/ उपर्ारप पर ककया गया व्यय।

3043. श्री एस. सेल वागनबनथे ी:

(क ) देश में वतचमान में ककतने आय ुवेददक महाववद्यालय कायचशील हैं और उनमें ककतने छात्र नामांककत 
हैं , तत् संथं ी राय य-वार /संघ राय य ्ेत्र-वार ब् यहरा क् या है;  
(ख) क् या सरकार पुडुर्ेरी में कोई आयुवेददक महाववद्यालय स  ा वपत करने पर ववर्ार कर रही है ; 
(गनब)   यदद हां, तो तत् संथं ी ब् यहरा क् या है; और  
(घ)   यदद नहीं, तो इसके क् या कारह हैं ? 
 
उत्तर 
आमुषयमांत्रीय(श्रीयसर्ाानांियसोणोर्वाल) 
 
(क ): ददनांक 17.03.2023 की स्स तत के अनुसार , शै्णहक सत्र 2022-23 के ललए देश में कायचशील 
आयुवेद महाववद्यालयों की संख्या और उनमें नामांककत ववद्यार् चयों की संख्या सांलग्नि पर दी गनबई है। 
 
(ख) से (घ): जन सवास्य रायय का ववषय होने के कारह , आयुवेद लश्ा के ललए नए शै्णहक संस ानों 
की स ापना संथंर् त रायय/संघ रायय ्ेत्र सरकारों के कायच्ेत्र में आता है। इसके अलावा , शै्णहक सत्र 
2023-24 के ललए भारतीय र्र्ककत्सा पद् तत राष्ट्रीय आयोगनब (एनसीआईएसएम ) को पुडुर्ेरी संघ रायय ्ेत्र 
सरकार से ऐसा कोई प्रसताव प्राप्त नहीं हुआ है।

(गनब)   सरकार द्वारा चर्ककत् सा की आय ुष पद्धतत को थाावा देने क े  सलए ववसभ् न राज् य सरकार  क े  प्रयास

उत्तर 
आमुषयमांत्रीय(श्रीयसर्ायकनांदयसो ोवाों ) 
 
(क ): 01.04.2021 की स्स् तत क े  अन ुसार , राज्य/संघ राज्य ्ेत्र सरकार  से प्राप्त आंकड  क े  अन ुसार,  
पुडुर्ेरी सहहत देश में आय ुव ेद, योगनब, प्राकृ ततक चर्ककत्सा , य ूनानी, ससद्ध और होमयोपी ी अस्पताल  की 
पद्धतत-वार और राज्य /संघ राज्य ्ेत्र-वार संखया सांों ग्नि-I पर दी  गनबई ही।  
 
(ख ): र्ूंकक जन स्वास््य राज्य का ववषय ही , इससलए चर्ककत् सक  और  परा-चर्ककत् सा कमचर्ायरय  क े  
असभलेख क े  अन ुर्ण  की प्रा समक स्जममेदारी संथंचधत राज्य /संघ राज्य ्ेत्र की सरकार  क े  कायच्ेत्र में 
आती ही। हालांकक , 01.01.2021 तक देश में आय ुष पंजीक ृ त चर्ककत्सक  (डॉक्टर ) की राज्य /संघ राज्य ्ेत्र 
थोडों/ पयरषद  द्वारा स ूचर्त राज्य/संघ राज्य ्ेत्र-वार संखया  सांों ग्नि-II पर दी गनबई ही।  
 
(गनब): आय ुष मंत्रालय एनएएम हदशातनद ेश  में तनहहत प्रावधान  क े  अन ुसार ववत्तीय सहायता प्रदान करक े  
राज्य/संघ राज्य ्ेत्र सरकार  क े  माध्यम से आय ुष चर्ककत्सा  पद्धततय  क े  ववकास और प्रर्ार क े  सलए 
राष्ट्ीीय आय ुष समशन (एनएएम) की क ें द्री य  प्रायोस्जत योजना को कायाचस््वत कर रहा ही। राष्ट्ीीय आय ुष 
समशन (एनएएम) अ्य थात  क े  सा -सा  तनमनसलखख त क े  सलए प्रावधान करता ही :- 
 
i. आय ुष स्वास््य एवं वेलनेस क ें द्र  
ii. प्रा समक स्वास््य क ें द्र  (पीएर्सी ), साम ुदातयक स्वास््य क ें द  (सीएर्सी ) और स्जला अस्पताल  
(डीएर् ) में आय ुष स ुववधाओं की सह -स् ापना  
iii. मौ‍जूदा एकल सरकारी आय ुष अस्पताल  का उ्नयन

(ख ): र्ूंकक जन  खवाख्य राज्य का ववषय है ,  सशलक ननयम/ कान ून क े  तहत , पररकजपपत ककसी भी

सरकारों  क े  कायचक्षेत्र में आता है। 
 
(ग) और (घ): जन  खवाख्य राज्य का ववषय होने क े  कारण , यूनानी शशक्षा क ें रों / संखथानों  की खथापना

करना बै और पारंपररक धर्ककत्सा में नैदाननक अभ्यास और प्रोटोकॉल बेतु मानक र्वकलसत करने बैं।  
 
भारतीय धर्ककत्सा एवं बो्योपैाी भेषजसंदबता आयोग (पीसीआईएम एंड एर्) ,

बसताक्षर ककए।

 क्मा यसामन औय उववयक  भंत्री मह फताने की कृऩा कयेंगे कक : 
 
(क) क्मा मह सच है कक डब्ल्मूएचओ ने हार ही भें बायत भें लनलभवत उन लनम्न स्तय की/दूवषत 
दवाओं औय कप लसयऩ क े  ववरुद्ध सावधालनमां  औय चेतावलनमां जायी की हैं जो गाम्म्फमा 
औय उज्फेककस्तान को लनमावत की गई थी; 
 
(ख) मकद हां, तो तत्संफंधी ब्लमौया क्मा है औय सयकाय द्वाया इस ऩय क्मा कायववाई की गई है;  
(ग) क्मा मह सच है कक घयेरू आऩूलतव की तुरना भें क े वर ववदेशों को लनमावत क े  उद्देश्म से देश भें 
लनलभवत दवाओं की गुणवत्ता को लनमंवत्रत कयने वारे भौजूदा लनमभों भें खालभमां हैं ; 
(घ) मकद हां, तो इससे संफंलधत भौजूदा कानूनों औय लनमभों का ब्लमौया क्मा है;

(ङ) इन गंबीय चूकों को योकने क े  लरए क्मा कायववाई प्रस्ताववत है?

क) औय (ख ) : ववषम वस्तु स्वास््म एवं ऩरयवाय क्माण ववबाग क े  अधीन क ें द्रीम औषलध भानक 
लनमंत्रण संगठन (सीडीएससीओ) से संफंलधत है।  सीडीएससीओ से प्राप्त जानकायी क े  अनुसाय, 
डब्ल्मूएचओ ने बायत भें वव लनलभवत कप लसयऩ क े  संफंध भें लनम्नलरम्खत दो लचककत्सा उत्ऩाद अरटव 
जायी ककए हैं जो गाम्म्फमा औय उज्फेककस्तान को लनमावत ककए गए थे:- 
  
i. गाम्म्फमा भें ऩहचाने गए भेडेन पाभावस्मुकटक्स लरलभटेड (हरयमाणा, बायत) द्वाया वव लनलभवत 
चाय उत्ऩादों नाभत: प्रोभेथेम्जन ओयर सॉ्मूशन, कोप े क्सभालरन फेफी कप लसयऩ, भैकॉप 
फेफी कप लसयऩ औय भैलिऩ एन को्ड लसयऩ ऩय कदनांक 05 -10-2022 को डब्ल्मूएचओ 
अरटव। 
ii. उज्फेककस्तान भें ऩहचाना ककए गए भैससव भैरयमन फामोटेक प्रा. लरलभटेड उत्तय प्रदेश, द्वाया 
वव लनलभवत दो उत्ऩादों नाभत: डीओक े  1 भैक्स लसयऩ (ऩैयालसटाभोर, गुइप े नेलसन औय

प े लनरफ्राइन हाइड्रोक्रोयाइड कप लसयऩ) औय एभिोनोर लसयऩ (एम्िोक्सोर लसयऩ)  ऩय 
कदनांक 11 -01-2023 को डब्ल्मूएचओ अरटव। 
 
गाम्म्फमा औय उज्फेककस्तान क े  भाभरे भें जांच का वववयण लनम्नानुसाय है: 
 
गाम्म्फमा भें रयऩोटव की गई भौतों क े  भाभरे भें, भैससव भेडेन पाभावस्मूकटक्स लरलभटेड 81, 
एचएसआईडीसी औद्योलगक ऺेत्र, क ुं डरी-131028, म्जरा सोनीऩत (हरयमाणा) भें याज्म औषलध 
लनमंत्रक, हरयमाणा क े  सभन्वम भें सीडीएससीओ द्वाया एक संमुक्त जांच की गई औय दवाइमों क े  
लनमंत्रण नभूने लरए गए औय ऺेत्रीम औषलध ऩयीऺण प्रमोगशारा, (आयडीटीएर) चंडीगढ़ को ऩयीऺण 
औय ववश्लेषण क े  लरए बेजे गए। आयडीटीएर चंडीगढ़ क े  सयकायी ववश्लेषक की रयऩोटव क े  अनुसाय,

एलथरीन ग्राइकॉर (ईजी) दोनों क े  लरए बी नकायात्भक ऩाए गए थे। 
 
मद्यवऩ, अच्छी ववलनभावण ऩम्ततमों भें ऩाए गए उ्रंघनों क े  आधाय ऩय, याज्म औषलध लनमंत्रक,

अलतरयक्त, भैससव भेडेन पाभावस्मुकटक्स लरलभटेड, सोनीऩत, हरयमाणा को कदनांक 11.10.2022 को 
जनकहत भें भैससव भेडेन पाभावस्मूकटक्स की सोनीऩत भें सबी वव लनभावण गलतववलधमों को तत्कार 
प्रबाव से योकने का आदेश जायी ककमा गमा है।  
 
इसी प्रकाय, उज्फेककस्तान क े  भाभरे भें, सीडीएससीओ ने याज्म औषलध लनमंत्रक, उत्तय प्रदेश क े

201301 (मूऩी) भें एक संमुक्त जांच की औय जांच क े  दौयान, दवा क े  नभूने वव लनभावण ऩरयसय से लरए

बेजे गए थे। इसक े  अलतरयक्त, कदनांक 09.01.2023 को याज्म राइसेंलसंग प्रालधकयण, उत्तय प्रदेश द्वाया

दवाइमों क े  नभूनों की ऩयीऺण रयऩोटव बेजी है, म्जसभें दवाइमों/कच्चे भार क े  24 नभूनों को "भानक 
गुणवत्ता का नहीं" घोवषत ककमा गमा था। म्जन 24 नभूनों को "भानक गुणवत्ता का नहीं" घोवषत 
ककमा गमा है भें से 22 नभूने लभरावटी/नकरी की श्रेणी भें आते हैं, जो योलगमों को गंबीय चोट 
ऩहुंचा सकते हैं। कदनांक 02.03.2023 को संफंलधत थाने भें प्राथलभकी  एपआईआय दजव की गई है 
औय तीन व्मवक्तमों को लगयफ्ताय ककमा गमा है।

के पचचात नीनत में पररवतजन ककए र्ाते हैं। एफडीआई नीनत के प्राविानों को पवलभन्न क्षेत्रों में उत्तरोत्तर 
उदार और सरल बनाया गया है।  इसके अलावा , एफडीआई रूट के तहत सरकार का अन ुमोदन मांगने वाले 
सभी प्रस्ताव अब राष्ट्रीय एकल खखड़की प्रणाली (एनएसडब्ल्यूएस) पो टजल पर प्रस्तुत ककए र्ाते हैं। 
 
रसायन क्षेत्र में ननवेश को बढावा देने और इसे स ुगम बनाने के ललए , सरकार ने संभापवत पररयोर्नाओं 
की पहचान करने , ननयलमत ननवेशक आउटरीच कायजक्रम आयोजर्त करने और इस क्षेत्र में नए  ननवेश को 
सुगम बनाने के ललए एक समपपजत पररयोर्ना पवकास सेल (पीडीसी ) भी स्थापपत ककया है।  साथ ही 
रसायन एवं पेरोरसायन पवभाग इस क्षेत्र में मेगा ननवेश आकपर्षजत करने के ललए “इंडडया केम”  और 
“वैजचवक रसायन और पेरोरसा यन पवननमाजण हब” पर सम्मेलन र्ैसे मेगा वैजचवक कायजक्रमों का दो साल 
में एक बार आयोर्न भी करता है।

(क) आज की तारीख में देश में प्रधान मंत्री भारतीय जन औषलध ऩररयोजना (ऩीएमबीजेऩी) क े

3065. डा. अमर ऩटनायक : 
   
 क्या रसायन और उववरक  मंत्री यह बताने की कृऩा करेंगे कक : 
 
(क) क्या दवा मूल्य लनधावरण प्रालधकरण ने 28 मार्व 2022 को उन अनुसूलर्त दवाओं क े  मूल्य 
में 10.7 प्रलतशत की वृवि की अनुमलत दी है जो मूल्य लनयंत्रण क े  अधीन हैं;  
(ख) यकद हां, तो ककतनी दवाओं क े  मूल्य में वृवि हुई है;  
(ग) क्या अनुसूलर्त दवाओं क े  मूल्य में वृवि प्रधानमंत्री भारतीय जन औषलध ऩररयोजना 
(ऩीएमबीजेऩी) क े  अंतगवत स्थावऩत जन औषलध क ें द्रों में उऩऱब्ध दवाओं ऩर भी ऱागू है; 
और 
(घ) यकद नहीं, तो इस बढोतरी क े  बाद प्रधानमंत्री भारतीय जन औषलध ऩररयोजना (ऩीएमबीजेऩी) 
क े  अंतगवत इन क ें द्रों में वबकने वाऱी दवाओं की कीमत को यथावत बनाए रखने क े  लऱए क्या 
उऩाय ककए गए हैं?  
 
उत्तर 
 
रसायन एवं  उववरक  राज्य मंत्री (श्री भगवंत खुबा) 
  (क ) और (ख): औषध ववभाग क े  तहत राष्ट्रीय औषध मूल्य लनधावरण प्रालधकरण (एनऩीऩीए) ने 
औषलध (मूल्य लनयंत्रण) आदेश, 2013 (डीऩीसीओ, 2013) क े  प्रावधानों क े  अनुसार क ै ऱेंडर वषव 2021 
क े  दौरान, वषव 2020 में इसी अवलध की तुऱना में सभी वस्तुओं क े  लऱए थोक मूल्य सूर्कांक 
(डब्ल्यूऩीआई) क े  आधार ऩर 898 अनुसूलर्त सम्ममश्रणों की अलधकतम कीमत को  सशोलधत करक े  
10.76607% सा बढा कदया है जो कदनांक 01.04.2022 से प्रभावी है। हाऱांकक , वव लनमावताओं द्वारा इन 
दवाओं की कीमतों में वृवि वाम्णम्ज्यक ववर्ार ऩर आधाररत है और यह बाजार की गलतशीऱता क े  
आधार ऩर कम या अनुमेय वृवि क े  समान हो सकती है।  
 
(ग) और (घ):  जन औषलध क ें द्रों क े  माध्यम से वबक्री की जाने वाऱी दवाओं सकहत अनुसूलर्त 
दवाओं क े  सभी वव लनमावताओं को दवाइयों की वबक्री अलधकतम मूल्य (डब्ल्यूऩीआई क े  आधार सकहत 
समय-समय ऩर यथसंशोलधत) क े  भीतर ही करनी होती है। इसक े  अऱावा , भारतीय औषध एवं 
लर्ककत्सा उऩकरण ब्यूरो (ऩीएमबीआई) यह सुलनम्ित करती है कक क ें द्रों क े  माध्यम से बेर्ी जाने 
वाऱी दवाओं की कीमतें खुऱे बाजार में उऩऱब्ध ब्ांडेड दवाओं की तुऱना में कम से कम 50% सस्ती 
हों।

(ख) क्मा क ें द्र सयकाय र्ीन से आमात हने वारे सकिम औषधीम साभग्री (एऩीआई) क े  लरए नए

तत्सॊफॊधी ब्मौया क्मा है? 
 
उत्तय  
यसामन एवॊ  उववयक  याज्म भॊत्री (श्री बगवॊत खुफा) 
 
(क):  बायतीम औषध उद्योग ववस्ताय-ऺेत्र क े  अनुसाय दुलनमा भें तीसये स्थान ऩय है। बायत दुलनमा भें 
सकिम पाभाव साभग्री (एऩीआई) मा थोक दवाओॊ क े  प्रभुख उत्ऩादकों भें से एक है। बायत ने ववत्तीम 
वषव 2021 -22 भें 33,320 कयोड़ रुऩमे की थोक औषलध/औषलध भध्मवती का लनमावत ककमा।  
हाराॉकक , देश ववलबन्न देशों से दवाओॊ क े  उत्ऩादन क े  लरए ववलबन्न थोक औषलध / एऩीआई का 
आमात बी कयता है औय देश भें ककए जा यहे थोक औषलध / एऩीआई क े  अलधकाॊश आमात आलथवक 
कायणों से होते हैं। बायत ने वषव 2021-22 भें 35,249 कयोड़ रुऩमे क े  एऩीआई औय थोक औषलध का 
आमात ककमा। अप्रैर, 2022 से जनवयी , 2023 तक क े  एऩीआई औय औषलध भध्मवती का आमात 
भूल्म 30337 कयोड़ रुऩमे है। (स्रोत: डीजीसीआईएस)

लरए कई उऩाम ककए हैं। इसक े  लरए कामविभ सॊफॊधी कामवकराऩ इस प्रकाय हैं;

(मैकटक्स) की  पानागढ़ यूररया इकाई ; र्ंबल फकटवलाइिसव एंड क े लमकल्स लललमटेड  (सीएफसीएल ) की  गड़ेपान-III 
यूररया इकाई ; रामागुंडम फकटवलाइिसव एंड क े लमकल्स लललमटेड  (आरएफसीएल ) की  रामागुंडम यूररया इकाई ; और 
कहन्िुस्तान उर्वरक एंड रसायन  लललमटेड  (एर्यूआरएल) की  3 यूररया इकाइयां  नामतिः गोरखपुर, लसंिरी और 
बरौनी हैं। इनमें से प्रत्येक इकाई  की  संस्थावपत यूररया उत्पािन क्षमता 12.7 लाख  मीकरक  टन प्रलत र्र्व है। इस 
प्रकार, इन इकाइयों  ने लमलकर  िेश की  मौिूिा स्र्िेशी यूररया उत्पािन क्षमता में 76.2 एलएमटी  प्रलत र्र्व की 
र्ृवर्द् की है।  
 
इसक े अलतररक्त, कोयला  गैसीकरण  मागव से 12.7 एलएमटी  प्रलत र्र्व क्षमता का एक  नया ग्रीनफील्ड 
यूररया संयंत्र स्थावपत करक े  एफसीआईएल  की  तलर्र इकाई  के  पुनरुर्द्ार के  ललए  28 अप्रैल 2021 को  एक  
वर्शेर् नीलत अलिसूलर्त की  गई है। 
 
सरकार ने  अपने उद्देश् यों में से एक स्र्िेशी यूररया उत्पािन को अलिकतम करने क े  उद्देश्य क े  साथ 25 
मई, 2015 को नई यूररया नीलत (एनयूपी) - 2015 अलिसूलर्त की है। एनयूपी-2015 क े  पररणामस् र्रूप 2014-
15 क े  िौरान हुए उत्पािन की तुलना में यूररया का 20-25 एलएमटीपीए  अलतररक् त उत् पािन हुआ है। 
 
िहां तक पीएंडक े  उर्वरकों का संबंि है , सरकार ने लनम् नललजखत किम उठाए  हैं:-  
 
1. मध्य भारत एग्रो प्रोडक्ट लललमटेड यूलनट-II, बांिा सागर, मध्य प्रिेश को 2.40 एल एमटी प्रलत र्र्व की 
संस्थावपत क्षमता क े  साथ डीएपी/एनपीक े  क े  उत्पािन की अनुमलत िी। 
2. मेससव कृष्‍टणा फॉस्क े म लललमटेड, मध्य प्रिेश को 3.30 एल एमटी प्रलत र्र्व की संस्थावपत क्षमता क े  साथ 
डीएपी/एनपीक े  क े  उत्पािन की अनुमलत िी। 
3. पीडीएम अथर्ा शीरे से प्राप्त पोटाश (0-0-14.5-0), िो 100% स् र्िेशी तौर पर वर्लनलमवत पोटाशयुक् त 
उर्वरक है, को पोर्कतत् र् आिाररत रािसहायता (एनबीएस) स् कीम क े  तहत शालमल ककया गया है।  
4. एसएसपी, िो एक स्र्िेशी रूप से वर्लनलमवत उर्वरक है, पर खरीफ और रबी 2022 -23 क े  ललए मालभाड़ा 
रािसहायता लागू की गई है।  
5. खान मंत्रालय, भारतीय भू -र्ैज्ञालनक सर्ेक्षण, मध्य प्रिेश, रािस्थान और उत्तर प्रिेश की सरकारों क े  
परामशव से घरेलू रूप से उपलब्ि उर्वरक खलनि संसािनों क े  खनन हेतु प्रयास ककए िा रहे हैं िो एक 
सतत प्रकिया है।

ववकास क े  पाइटोपाभावस्मुकटकर भागव ऩय काभ कयने की ऺभता औय ववशेषऻता ववकलसत की है।

आकद क े  लरए नए उऩर्ायों की खोज से जुडी जकटर सभस्माओं को हर कयने का प्रमास  सहमोग 
कयक े  औय साभूकहक रूऩ से कय सकते हैं।  
ओएसडीडी वतवभान भें टीफी औय भरेरयमा क े  लरए नई दवाओं की खोज ऩय क ें कित है। ओएसडीडी 
सहमोगी रूऩ से वैऻालनकों क े  लरए उऩरधध जैववक , आनुवंलशक औय यासामलनक जानकायी को एकत्र 
कयता है ताकक दवाओं की खोज भें तेजी राने क े  लरए इसका उऩमोग ककमा जा सक े । मह वैऻालनकों , 
डॉक्टयों, टेक्नोक्र े ट, छात्रों औय ववववध ववशेषऻता वारे अन्म रोगों क े  लरए एक साझा उद्देश्म क े  लरए
